page: Microsoft Azure D16plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz, with a single thread per core. The memory configuration is 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark results show strong memory performance, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 307.54 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 124.58 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Single-threaded gzip compression is also highly efficient at 33.08 GB/sec. Standard CPU benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core (33160.55) and Geekbench multi-core (14736.0), fall within the average range. Large-model LLM prompt processing is a relative bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% at 24.62 tokens/sec, though small-model text generation remains strong at 263.31 tokens/sec.

The ARM64 architecture combined with a low memory-to-core ratio provides a cost-efficient profile for workloads that prioritize raw integer compute and local storage speed over large memory footprints. The bundled 945 GB NVMe SSD makes it suitable for local caching, web serving, and lightweight database operations. This instance is well-suited for software compilation, static web serving, and containerized microservices that benefit from dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading overhead.
